_comment: Routing config only — endpoint, model id, reasoning effort, profile membership. Carries NO quality scores: a stale ranking is worse than none. Availability is MEASURED by `review.py --list`, which probes each provider live; a key being set is not availability. All reviewers use DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (64000) unless they set max_output_tokens: reasoning tokens come out of the answer's budget, and at 16000 a large review returned no content at all. Prices in _cost are per-million-token budgeting hints, not routing inputs; later owner decisions and unmeasured prices are noted on the seats.

_profiles.plan: TWO contrasting models, never escalated. For acceptance criteria and designs, BEFORE code exists. Owner decision 2026-10-12: astra and kimi-k3, OpenAI and Moonshot, because the orchestrator writing plans is a Claude model. Pair under review: a plan-review benchmark decides it (owner decision 2026-10-18).
_profiles.fast: luna and haiku-5.5; cheapest implementation panel, the first tier of --escalate (owner decision 2026-10-12).
_profiles.standard: luna, kimi-k2.7-code and sonnet-5.5; the usual fixed implementation panel. Escalating from fast retains its verdicts and adds kimi-k2.7-code and sonnet-5.5.
_profiles.deep: standard + sol. Final --escalate tier, or a fixed --profile deep panel. astra is NOT here since 2026-09-24: it writes the code now, and an author does not review itself.
_profiles.committee: committee.py members, separate from gate profiles. Owner decision 2026-10-13: deepseek-v4-pro, gemini-argon and sonnet-5.5, three model makers. DeepSeek sits in no gate profile.
_profiles.tiebreak: Committee divergence only: the ONE enabled reviewer whose only profile is tiebreak rules on existing positions. committee.py selects it by this profile, never by name or model. Not a gate tier or a committee membership profile. sol-tiebreak since 2026-09-28, replacing astra-xhigh because astra authors the code it would rule on (ARC-755).
_profiles.planning: committee.py open --profile planning, for the hanig-project design step. Owner decision 2026-10-18: astra and gemini-argon. Separate from the step-back committee because committee.py refuses a session whose member authored the work, and astra writes the code.

_effort_null_is_deliberate: Measured 2026-09-19, three samples per cell against a real 120-line diff at a 16000 cap: glm-5.3 at effort=high burned the ENTIRE budget on reasoning and returned zero characters in 3 of 3 samples, at effort=low in 2 of 3, and at effort=null returned a 4581-character review for $0.016 in 3 of 3. kimi-k2.7-code spends ~12k completion tokens at every level, so effort changes nothing but price: high cost 83% more and returned slightly LESS answer. A null effort here is therefore deliberate and load-bearing, not an omission. Setting one on either reviewer makes the gate pay more for less, and on glm-5.3 for nothing at all. glm-5.3 was dropped from the roster on 2026-09-28; its measurements stay here as the evidence for the rule. kimi-k2.7-code keeps effort null.
_output_budget_rule: Every ENABLED reviewer must declare max_output_tokens explicitly and must carry a STRUCTURED _max_output_tokens_accepted record: date, max_output_tokens, provider, model, outcome and a positive output_tokens. tests/test_reviewer_budgets.py compares those typed fields to the reviewer's own configuration by exact equality. It was free text matched by substring for one round, and the gate refused that correctly: "completed a 1280000-token request via openrouterx for z-ai/glm-5.3-variant" satisfied substring checks for 128000, openrouter and z-ai/glm-5.3. English commentary belongs in _max_output_tokens, not in the thing a test parses. The rule exists because the 64000 shared default is not a safe default for a reasoning model -- it silently starved glm-5.3 and then kimi-k2.7-code (ARC-689). ARC-689 now records a starved reviewer as REVIEW_INCOMPLETE and gives it no judgment; it still spends resource budget and prevents a pass. Inheriting the default is therefore not permitted for an enabled reviewer, which is why any reviewer must be measured before it is enabled. Acceptance is per MODEL: 128000 completing for gpt-6-astra says nothing about gpt-6-sol. output_tokens is required and must be positive because a provider ACCEPTING a budget is not the same fact as a reviewer RETURNING usable output, and it was the second fact that motivated this change. STILL OWED, and not claimed here: these records are transcribed by hand from measured runs. Nothing generates them from the probe, so the test checks that a record is well formed and self-consistent, never that the run happened.
_dropped: 2026-09-28 by owner decision: glm-5.3 (slowest reviewer in 18 saved gate runs, 408 s average, most expensive open model, starved at the old default in ARC-689), kimi-k3 (disabled since 2026-08-27, never measured) and astra-xhigh (the tie-breaker seat moved to sol-tiebreak). Their entries are in git history. kimi-k3 rejoins plan by owner decision 2026-10-12 after a successful live xhigh probe.
_family: A seat's `family` lets resolve_models.py move it to a newer POINT RELEASE at project start: a listed id whose vendor path equals `vendor` and whose name is `prefix` + version (N, or N + `separator` + M) + `suffix`, with major equal to `major`, above the pinned `model`, whose probe passes. `major` is the owner's ceiling; raising it is a reviewed change to this file. The resolved choice lives in a per-project snapshot under the state home, never here; see docs/plan-model-resolution.md. The seat NAME is a label and does not change when the model does. A named_version with major 0 is an exact named pin, not an ordered numeric family; no automatic upgrade is admitted.
